subject: ventures/consignment-markdown-planner
professional: the owner/manager of a resale consignment shop who sets markdown ladders (30/60/90-day colour-tag schedules), consignor splits paid on the sold price, and the end-of-contract policy (return, donate, or item becomes shop property). First checks: is the split applied to the marked-down sold price so the consignor shares the markdown, does the tool show what each consignor will be paid, does it model what happens to unsold items at contract expiry, and do the recommendations survive a plausible range of markdown response, since nobody in a small shop knows their lift.

evidence.correctness: Independent Python brute force (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/4c488086-781e-5ba3-9f2e-f786d86a9ac5/scratchpad/consign/indep.py), written from the stated model (geometric weekly hazard, rate = min(cap, base x (1 + lift x d/10)), shop gets share x price x (1-d), shelf cost per alive week, handling once) and enumerating all 1,820 non-decreasing 12-week schedules over {0,10,25,40,50} instead of the engine's DP. Against `node cli.mjs plan fixtures/items.csv`: all 10 items' best net, schedule, sell-through, fixed-rule net and never-markdown net identical (e.g. blazer 26.76 / 81% / 25.45 / 23.61; oak table -0.64 at 40% all 12 weeks); totals plan 152.58, fixed 137.00, never 113.63, slow-season 75.47; kept-only 157.93, uplift 8.25 vs fixed, 22.56 vs never; expected consignor payout on the blazer 49.23; tee break-even price 17.93 and share 59.8%; oak table break-even price 163.78 -- all identical. The arithmetic and the optimiser are right. Not 4: `--weeks 2.5` (and a fractional value typed in the page's weeks box) crashes with the internal message 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 0)' because readOptions (engine.mjs:99) does not require an integer, while the per-row weeks field does.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features run end to end: exact best schedule per item (verified above), decline at intake with the price and shop share that flip it (verified), fixed 30/60 rule and never-markdown comparisons (verified), slow-season re-check at 60% of rates (verified 75.47), JSON output, stdin, levels/handling/cap/lift options, 200-item limit, browser page using the same engine.mjs, usage counter with opt-out/DNT/GPC, explainer page linked both ways and in the sitemap. Consignor payout is computed (engine.mjs:129) but appears only in --json and the explainer prose; the page table (index.html:72) and CLI text never show it. No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/consignment-markdown-planner && node --test '*.test.mjs': 29/29 pass, 0.2 s. The DP is checked against brute force on 150 random items, a strong oracle. Seven seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py on engine.mjs: DP continuation without (1-q) caught; consignor payout using share instead of (1-share) caught; fixed-rule 50% step moved a week caught. SURVIVED: the weekly sell cap removed (min(o.cap,..) -> min(1,..)); the accept boundary >= 0 -> > 0; the slow-season scale removed entirely (o.slow/100 -> 1), i.e. a whole user-visible column and the slow-season total can be wrong with every test green; the slow-season warning threshold < 0 -> < -1. 3 of 7 caught.
evidence.craft: Read engine.mjs (242 lines), cli.mjs (95), usage.mjs (80), index.html script block, all four test files. Pure engine, no dependencies, parse errors carry line numbers, storage wrapped against SecurityError, output escaped. Defects: fractional global weeks crashes with a TypeError text shown to the user (engine.mjs:99); quoted CSV names ("Silk, blazer") produce a misleading 'price must be a number' error rather than a CSV-quote message (engine.mjs:59; documented as 'avoid commas'); the CLI prints a kept-only total in the summary ($157.93) and an all-items total in the footer ('Plan $152.58', cli.mjs:79) with no label saying which, and the page's totals table mixes kept-only rows with an all-items slow-season row (index.html:161, labelled). The fixed rule always uses 25%/50% even when the user's allowed levels exclude them, so 'plan never worse than the fixed rule' is not guaranteed for custom levels (it held on the cases tried).
evidence.claims: Backed: 'exact best schedule ... checked against every non-decreasing schedule' (engine.test.mjs:39 and my brute force); explainer worked-example figures 63%, $23.61, $25.45, $26.76, 81%, $49.23, tee -$1.63, $17.93, 59.8% all reproduce; 'up to 200 items' (MAX_ITEMS); 'nothing is uploaded' (no fetch/XHR/beacon in index.html, engine.mjs or usage.mjs); disclaimer (no warranty, not financial/tax/legal advice) on both pages; served llms.txt clean (node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin; the github.io links in the source are rewritten at deploy). FAIL: the explainer is titled and described as '30/60/90-day schedule math' and its FAQ (how-should...html:50) says 'Is a 30/60/90-day markdown schedule good enough? ... The planner compares it with the best schedule' -- the planner has no 90-day step; it compares only a 2-step 30/60 (25% at week 5, 50% at week 9) rule. PARTIAL: the explainer quotes the consignor payout but the tool's page never shows it. PARTIAL: README Privacy says 'no analytics vendor' but does not mention the local usage counter the page footer discloses. The headline 'what a fixed rule leaves on the table' rests on the uncited default lift 0.35: at lift 0.1 the same fixture's best plan is never-mark-down for every kept item and the fixed rule loses $18.38; the page does call the rates 'your estimates', so this is a partial, not a fail.
evidence.fitness: Walked the owner's job with the fixture. It answers 'should I take this item in, and at what split' well, and the break-even price/share is a useful intake rule. It falls short of the weekly job: (1) no consignor payout per item or per consignor on the page, the number a consignment owner reconciles every month; (2) unsold items at contract end are worth zero -- no return-to-consignor, donation, or abandoned-becomes-shop-property value, which in practice is the 90-day end of the ladder and changes how deep late markdowns should go; (3) per-item weekly schedules do not map onto how shops actually run markdowns (one colour-tag ladder by intake month), and there is no grouping of items into a single shared ladder; (4) the owner has no way to estimate base rate or lift from a POS export, and the answer flips with lift (0.1 -> hold price; 0.2 -> first markdown week 5; 0.35 -> 10% off from week 1, brute-force check), so the tool tells a shop with unknown lift little it can act on without a sensitivity view.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard consignment practice (split paid on actual sold price so the consignor bears the markdown pro rata; fixed 30/60/90 ladders tied to a 60- or 90-day contract; end-of-term pickup/donate/shop-ownership clauses) and the markdown-optimisation literature (finite-horizon DP over a non-increasing price path, e.g. Gallego and van Ryzin style models). Right: split on sold price, monotone price path, exact DP, shelf-slot opportunity cost and handling, intake break-even. Departures: (1) no end-of-term residual value or expiry action, which a consignment model needs more than a retail one; (2) constant hazard with no item ageing, so the only reason to deepen is the horizon; (3) a single uncited default lift (0.35/10% off) under which 10% off raises weekly expected revenue (1.35 x 0.9 = 1.215), so the tool recommends marking 5 of 6 kept fixture items down from week 1 -- in consignment that means re-tagging below the price agreed with the consignor, which most agreements do not allow and the finding text does not flag; (4) the comparison ladder is 30/60 only, not the 30/60/90 ladder the page names.

mutations.change: evaluate(item, best.discounts, o, o.slow / 100) -> evaluate(item, best.discounts, o, 1)

defects.what: The explainer is titled and described as '30/60/90-day schedule math' and its FAQ says the planner compares a 30/60/90-day schedule with the best one; the engine scores only a 2-step 30/60 rule (25% from week 5, 50% from week 9) with no 90-day step, so the 'dollars the fixed rule leaves behind' are not for the ladder the page names.

Unsold items at the end of the consignment term are valued at zero: no return-to-consignor, donation, or abandoned-becomes-shop-property (100% share) value, which is the end of a 30/60/90 ladder in practice and changes how deep the last markdowns should go. README:29 and index.html:97 state donation value is not modelled, so this is a disclosed limit, but return and shop-ownership at expiry are not mentioned.

The recommendation hinges on a single uncited default lift (0.35 per 10% off): at 0.1 the best plan holds full price, at 0.35 it marks 5 of 6 kept fixture items down from week 1 (below the consignor-agreed tag), with no sensitivity view and no note that a week-1 markdown usually needs the consignor's agreement.
Slow-season re-check, the cap and the accept boundary are untested: removing the slow-season scale entirely, removing the weekly cap, or changing accept >= 0 to > 0 leaves all 29 tests green.
Consignor payout is computed but shown only in --json and in the explainer prose; the page table and CLI text omit it, though it is the figure a consignment owner reconciles.

A fractional global weeks value (--weeks 2.5, or 2.5 typed in the page's weeks box) is accepted by readOptions and then crashes in bestSchedule, surfacing 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 0)'.
CLI text prints a kept-only total in the summary ($157.93) and an all-items total in the footer ('Plan $152.58', fixed rule $137.00) without saying which base each uses.
README Privacy says 'no analytics vendor' and omits the local usage counter (plan_run, example_loaded) and its opt-out that the page footer discloses.

verdict: The maths is right: an independent brute force over all 1,820 twelve-week schedules reproduces every per-item net, schedule, sell-through, fixed-rule and never-markdown figure, the totals (152.58 / 137.00 / 113.63 / slow 75.47), the intake break-evens (tee $17.93 or 59.8% share) and the consignor payout ($49.23) exactly, and the DP is tested against brute force. It misses the bar on verification and claims: the slow-season re-check, the weekly cap and the accept boundary can all be broken with every test green (3 of 7 seeded mutants caught), and the explainer sells '30/60/90-day schedule math' while the tool only scores a 2-step 30/60 rule. For a consignment owner it is an intake-screening aid more than a markdown planner: it never shows consignor payouts, values unsold items at contract end at zero, and its verdict flips from 'hold price' to 'mark down from week 1' across lift 0.1 to 0.35, with an uncited 0.35 default.
